title: Queen against rook: the Philidor position
summary: Winning the rook with the queen: cut the black king off to the edge, beat the second- or third-rank defence and reach the Philidor position, with Black to move, within the fifty-move rule.
history:
Queen against rook looks like an easy ending, because the queen is worth much more than the rook. But a rook glued to its king defends for a long time, and whoever does not know the plan runs into the fifty-move rule.

The Frenchman {{Philidor|francois-andre-philidor}} analysed this ending in the 1777 edition of his book and showed the position that now bears his name: with Black to move, the rook cannot escape.
practice: The Philidor position with White to move.
key.black: Philidor position: Black to move loses the rook.
part.philidor.title: Philidor's position
part.philidor.summary: With Black to move, every move makes things worse: the rook that leaves its king falls to a fork, a pin or checks up to the fork square.
ex.philidorAssessment01: Play as White and win the rook. It is on g2, far from the black king, which is on a2, and undefended.
ex.philidorAssessment01.hint: Look for a check that attacks the rook at the same time.
ex.philidorAssessment01.solution: 1.Qd5+ checks along the diagonal to a2 and attacks the rook on g2 along the other diagonal: it is a fork. After 1...Kb2, 2.Qxg2 wins the rook. No other move wins the rook as fast.
ex.philidorAssessment01.r1: 1...Kb2. The king steps out of check; a1, a3 or b1 would be the same. The rook is left undefended.
part.tempo.title: Handing over the move
part.tempo.summary: The Philidor position only wins with Black to move: when it is your move, the queen triangle hands the move over without stalemating the king.
ex.tempoAssessment01: Play as White. The black king is on b8, with the rook on b7; your king is on c6, and the queen on c1. Find the fastest move to the win.
ex.tempoAssessment01.hint: Which position is the queen looking for, and whose move should it be?
ex.tempoAssessment01.solution: 1.Qf4+: in three moves the queen returns to the Philidor position with Black to move. If 1...Ka8, 2.Qa4+ Kb8 3.Qa5, and Black is in zugzwang. 1.Qh1 also wins just as fast: 1...Ka8 2.Qa1+ Kb8 3.Qa5, by the lesson's triangle.
part.segunda.title: Defence on the second rank
part.segunda.summary: With the rook next to the king on the second rank, the queen's checks bring your king close until the Philidor position; if the rook gets careless, the pin or the fork wins it.
ex.segundaAssessment01: Play as White. The black king is on d8, with the rook beside it, on c7; your king is on e5, and the queen on b5. Find the fastest move to the win.
ex.segundaAssessment01.hint: After each of your moves, count how many moves Black has left that do not lose the rook.
ex.segundaAssessment01.solution: 1.Kd6, without check, against the second-rank defence: your king stands in front of the black king and attacks the rook, which the black king protects. Black is in zugzwang: if the rook leaves c7, the queen mates on b8 or on d7, or the rook falls. That leaves 1...Kc8, and 2.Qa5 leaves Black without a good move again. The check on b8 also wins, but only later: the black king escapes via d7.
part.terceira.title: Third-rank defence
part.terceira.summary: The rook on the third rank shuts out the king: the queen takes its squares until the rook returns to the second rank, or wins it with a fork if it moves away from the king.
ex.terceiraAssessment01: Play White. The black king is on b8, and the rook is on e6, on Black's third rank, far from the king; your king is on b5, and the queen is on g2. Win the rook.
ex.terceiraAssessment01.hint: The rook is unprotected: which check also attacks it?
ex.terceiraAssessment01.solution: 1.Qg8+, a fork: check along the eighth rank and an attack on the rook on e6, along the g8-f7-e6 diagonal. The king steps out of check without reaching e6, and 2.Qxe6 wins the rook; if 1...Re8, 2.Qxe8+.
part.borda.title: From the center to the edge
part.borda.summary: The queen cuts off the black king, and your king advances behind it to the edge, leaving the rook no skewer, fork or trade.
part.convert.title: From the center to the won rook
part.convert.summary: The whole game: cut off the king, recognise the defence, reach the Philidor position and win the rook within the fifty-move rule.
ex.bordaAssessment01: Play as White. The black king is on f3, with the rook beside it, on e2. Find the queen move that starts driving it to the edge.
ex.bordaAssessment01.hint: Look for a move without check that takes a whole file away from the black king.
ex.bordaAssessment01.solution: 1.Qd1, without check: the queen takes the d-file away from the black king and pins the e2 rook to the king on f3. The rook cannot move, and only the black king can play. The checks also win, but they do not cut off the black king, and the win is further away.
ex.convertAssessment01: Play White. It is move 61, and there has been no capture for 40 moves: under the fifty-move rule, 10 are left. The black king is on e4, and the rook on h2, far from it.
ex.convertAssessment01.hint: Only the shortest path fits in the 10 moves. Look for checks that bring the queen to the fork square.
ex.convertAssessment01.solution: 1.Qg4+, along the fourth rank. If the king goes to e5, e3 or d3, 2.Qg3+ checks and attacks the rook on h2: it is the fork, and 3.Qxh2. If it goes to d5, 2.Qf5+ and 3.Qf4+ make the same fork. The rook falls by move 64, within the limit.
